name: Shingle Court cottage
role: Low courtyards, roof gaps and the lower edges of views
design: A LOW WIDE courtyard cottage, just ONE FULL STOREY plus a modest roof loft, approximately 8.5 m wide by 5.5 m deep. Broad pale limestone and chalk-plaster walls, a long warm terracotta pitched roof with two small low dormers, and one short chimney stack at an end. Keep its roof ridge and walls much lower in proportion to its width than the taller town houses. One muted teal entry, three small domestic ground windows, restrained oak eave brackets and a plain timber garden gate tight against one end. At the rear a shallow covered kitchen stoop, rain barrel and a small herb bench explain daily use; the opposite side remains simple masonry. A few repaired tiles and a weathered shutter are enough detail. No second full storey, tower, public hall, ornate pavilion or sprawling garden. Make a warm modest dwelling that can sit below a taller street without hiding it.
